public_rationale: In March 2024 the speaker said AI had about three quarters to prove itself before an 'apocalypse' that would savage the revenues of the biggest tech companies. That puts the collapse around the end of 2024. To allow for reporting lag, I kept the window open to mid-2025. In that time the largest tech firms' revenues grew. Microsoft's revenue rose 12% in the December 2024 quarter, and growth sped up to 18% by the June 2025 quarter. Alphabet's revenue rose 12% in Q4 2024. No AI-driven revenue collapse happened in the window, so the forecast is contradicted.
limitations: Only Microsoft and Alphabet releases are cited. Other big tech firms are not checked one by one.
The window end (mid-2025) is my reading. The speaker gave no explicit lag.

conditions: unless AI proves itself within three quarters

statement.excerpt: I believe that artificial intelligence has three quarters to prove itself before the apocalypse comes, and when it does, it will be that much worse, savaging the revenues of the biggest companies in tech.

from_speaker: artificial intelligence has three quarters to prove itself
savaging the revenues of the biggest companies in tech
our_interpretation: Plain reading: a firm prediction that an AI bust would arrive about three quarters after the March 2024 post (around the end of 2024) and would sharply cut the revenues of the largest tech companies.
'Biggest companies in tech' means the largest US tech firms by market value whose revenue is tied to AI: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia, and Apple.
'Savaging the revenues' means steep, broad year-over-year declines in these firms' reported total revenue. Slower growth alone does not count.
The collapse was due around end-2024. Revenue reports lag, so the window runs to mid-2025 (quarters ending by 2025-06-30). This gives the speaker extra time.
I do not treat the claim as conditional on a separate test of whether AI 'proved itself'. The sentence says the apocalypse 'comes' and 'will' savage revenues.
criteria.support_condition: Most of the largest tech companies report steep year-over-year revenue declines in quarters ending between late 2024 and 2025-06-30, linked to falling AI demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The largest tech companies report rising year-over-year revenue through the quarters ending late 2024 to mid-2025, with no broad AI-driven revenue collapse.

Microsoft Corp. today announced the following results for the quarter ended December 31,

evidence.explanation: Microsoft's revenue grew 12% in the quarter ending about three quarters after the post. That is the opposite of a revenue collapse.

evidence.explanation: Alphabet's revenue rose 12% in Q4 2024. The release says the figures are unaudited. Another of the biggest tech firms shows growth, not savaged revenue.
